# Needs assessment: first-line immunotherapy plus chemotherapy in advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer, by mismatch repair status

<!-- Demo draft: generated by Claude (Anthropic) from prompt_pack.md, then checked with `python run.py verify`. -->

## Background and burden

Standard first-line chemotherapy for advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer has been paclitaxel plus carboplatin [PMID:36972022].
The Cancer Genome Atlas described four molecular subtypes of endometrial cancer with different prognoses, and a simplified classifier groups tumors as POLE, mismatch repair deficient, p53 abnormal and no specific molecular profile [PMID:36399812].
In a Canadian cohort of 1357 evaluable patients, 380 tumors (28.0%) were mismatch repair deficient [PMID:36241860].

## Current evidence

In the RUBY trial, 494 patients were randomized to dostarlimab or placebo plus carboplatin-paclitaxel, and 118 (23.9%) had dMMR/MSI-H tumors [PMID:36972026].
In the dMMR/MSI-H population, progression-free survival at 24 months was 61.4% with dostarlimab versus 15.7% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.28) [PMID:36972026].
At the second interim analysis, RUBY met its overall survival endpoint in the overall population (HR 0.69), with a larger reduction in the risk of death in the dMMR/MSI-H population (HR 0.32) [PMID:38866180].
In NRG-GY018, which enrolled 816 patients, 12-month progression-free survival in the dMMR cohort was 74% with pembrolizumab versus 38% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.30) [PMID:36972022].
In the pMMR cohort of NRG-GY018, median progression-free survival was 13.1 months with pembrolizumab and 8.7 months with placebo (hazard ratio 0.54) [PMID:36972022].
Overall survival in NRG-GY018 remained immature, with hazard ratios favoring pembrolizumab in both mismatch repair-proficient (0.79) and mismatch repair-deficient (0.55) disease [PMID:40044930].
In DUO-E, 718 patients were randomized, and progression-free survival improved with durvalumab (HR 0.71) and with durvalumab plus olaparib (HR 0.55) versus control [PMID:37864337].
In the dMMR subgroup of DUO-E the progression-free survival hazard ratios were 0.42 and 0.41, while in the pMMR subgroup they were 0.77 and 0.57 [PMID:37864337].
Safety: severe and serious adverse events were more frequent with dostarlimab than with placebo in RUBY [PMID:36972026].
A network meta-analysis of four trials involving 2577 patients found dostarlimab plus chemotherapy most beneficial for survival in dMMR/MSI-H disease and durvalumab plus chemotherapy with olaparib in pMMR/MSS disease [PMID:38901970].

## Practice gaps

Clinicians should know each patient's mismatch repair status before first-line systemic therapy, because the magnitude of benefit from adding a PD-1 or PD-L1 inhibitor differs markedly between dMMR and pMMR disease [PMID:36972026, PMID:36972022, PMID:37864337].
All endometrial cancers should undergo basic molecular classification that includes mismatch repair status [PMID:36399812], yet in 2016 mismatch repair immunohistochemistry was performed at diagnosis in only 42% of a Canadian cohort, and 54.7% of mismatch repair deficient tumors had not been tested [PMID:36241860].
Inconsistent, non-reflexive testing led to missed opportunities for Lynch syndrome diagnosis and for immune blockade in mismatch repair deficient disease [PMID:36241860].

## Evidence gaps

Overall survival data in pMMR disease are still immature or reported only as a trend, so the size of the survival benefit in this larger subgroup is uncertain [PMID:40044930, PMID:38866180].
Whether patients with mismatch repair deficient disease can safely omit chemotherapy is being tested in the phase III DOMENICA trial of dostarlimab versus chemotherapy [PMID:40323277].
No head-to-head trial has compared the available immunotherapy-chemotherapy regimens; comparative conclusions rely on network meta-analysis [PMID:38901970].

## Proposed learning objectives

1. Order and interpret mismatch repair testing for every patient with newly diagnosed advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer.
2. Compare progression-free and overall survival outcomes of immunotherapy plus chemotherapy regimens in dMMR versus pMMR disease.
3. Discuss immune-related and overall toxicity with patients when selecting first-line therapy.

## Assessment questions

1. In the dMMR/MSI-H population of RUBY, what was the 24-month progression-free survival with dostarlimab plus chemotherapy? A) 36.1% B) 61.4% C) 74% D) 15.7%. Answer: B. Rationale: 61.4% with dostarlimab versus 15.7% with placebo [PMID:36972026].
2. Which statement about the pMMR cohort of NRG-GY018 is correct? A) No PFS benefit B) Median PFS 13.1 vs 8.7 months C) OS was significantly improved D) The trial excluded pMMR patients. Answer: B. Rationale: median progression-free survival was 13.1 months with pembrolizumab and 8.7 months with placebo [PMID:36972022].
3. According to the SGO practice statement, which assessment should be part of basic molecular classification of all endometrial cancers? A) HER2 only B) Mismatch repair status C) ARID1A only D) None. Answer: B. Rationale: all endometrial cancers should undergo basic molecular classification including mismatch repair status [PMID:36399812].
